comments.author: experiment-repo
comments.body: Assignment pushed (3e02340): `figures/` is yours. The pilot (job-c703b04670) started 10:10:23 UTC and ends ~10:19:30 UTC. When it does I will push `results/pilot.json` (raw), `results/running_estimate.csv` (columns: elapsed_s, samples, estimate, ci95_lo/hi per checkpoint, true_pi_band_lo/hi = pi ± 1.96·4·sqrt(q(1−q)/n) with q=pi/4, z_vs_true_pi) and `results/estimate.json` (final estimate, Wald and Wilson 95% CI), then answer here and close. Notes for the figure: checkpoints are ~10 s apart, so the first is at ~10^6–10^7 samples (log x axis); points are cumulative estimates, hence strongly correlated — a band around pi (the expected ±1.96σ_n funnel) is more honest than independent error bars. Leaving this open until the data is pushed.

comments.author: experiment-repo
comments.body: Pushed in 9af86d4f20cf274be0a6455fab91fd58c83a3423: `results/running_estimate.csv` (55 checkpoints, 1e5 → 1 759 200 000 samples; columns elapsed_s, samples, estimate, ci95_lo, ci95_hi, true_pi_band_lo, true_pi_band_hi, z_vs_true_pi), raw `results/pilot.json`, final values in `results/estimate.json` and `results/README.md`. Final: 3.1415539, 95% CI [3.1414772, 3.1416307] (Wald; Wilson identical to <3e-9), n = 1 759 200 000. What the figure must show: the running estimate converging on pi with every checkpoint inside the ±1.96σ_n band around pi (max |z| = 1.40), and the final CI covering pi (z = −0.99). Note the first checkpoint is at 1e5 samples and the second at 3.1e7, so a log x axis leaves a gap between them; that is the data, not a missing range. Generate from the CSV by reading it (no hard-coded values).

issue.body:
